annotations.text:
THREE DIRECTIONS — same dashboard, same content, three different ideas about what BrightCV should feel like.

Each differs in palette AND in interface: navigation model, density, and how the CV list is presented. Pick one and I'll build the CV builder and the phone screens in it.

INK & MARIGOLD — editorial
Warm paper (#FAF6EF), near-black ink, marigold (#C9741A) and a deep forest green. Instrument Serif + IBM Plex Sans. Flat: hairline rules instead of shadows, a masthead, and the CV list set as a proper table.

Why: a CV is a document, so the app reads like good print.
Tradeoff: the flat, rule-based style leans formal — less obviously friendly than C, and the table needs care on a phone.

MIDNIGHT STUDIO — dark tool
Deep indigo (#0F1220 / #181C2E) with an electric lime (#C6F050) and coral for attention. Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Sans. Left rail navigation, compact panels, data forward.

Why: reads as a serious, modern working tool; the lime makes one action unmistakable on every screen.
Tradeoff: dark-first is a big shift for a document app, and the white CV preview will always sit hard against the dark chrome.

CLAY & SAGE — warm and human
Sand (#F4EBE0), clay (#B4553A), sage (#63775C), honey. Bricolage Grotesque + Karla. Floating pill nav, 26px radii, one centred column, lots of room.

Why: closest to the calm, forgiving tone you wrote into the brief — the least intimidating for someone job-hunting.
Tradeoff: the generous spacing costs screen real estate, which the dense CV builder will feel most.
